title_en: The Ubhavalo -- a traditional song-form (the printed heading reads Ubhavalo; exact sense of the name is unclear)
translation:
Here begins the holy Ubhavalo ||26||

1. Lovely, lovely is he -- the King of Vaikunth has been found! Fair is the bridegroom of Rukmini; he has wiped out sins from their very seat. Take the name of Narayan. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm. My Govind-Ram, I take refuge at your feet.

2. I read and read, and mastered all four Vedas; I lost myself on the path of ritual works and went wandering. I never came to know the secret of bhakti (devotion). Caught up in many things, I bow my head. Repeat the name...

3. O gods, O gods -- the God of gods has been found, the Master of all Vaikunth! Serve him, serve him -- he who tore Hiranyakashipu apart. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm.

4. He wore, he wore the yellow silken robe, and put on a garland of gunja berries. This cowherd lad took up the bamboo flute, and work and household were all forgotten. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm.

5. Enchanted, enchanted were the thirty-three crore gods; enchanted were the cowherd women of Gokul. This cowherd lad, this herdsman boy, has put an end to the dwelling in the womb -- he has lifted us out of the mother's lap of rebirth. Repeat the name...

6. Lakshmi, Lakshmi -- the husband of Lakshmi has been found, Damodar, the grinder of poverty to dust. Filled with joy, filled with joy are your saints, when your glance falls upon them. Repeat the name of Shri Padmanabh, the yellow-robed Parbrahm.

Here the holy Ubhavalo is complete ||26||
